topology: PC1 192.168.10.10/24 connects directly to R1 Gi0/0 192.168.10.1. R1 Gi0/1 10.0.12.1/30 faces R2 Gi0/0 10.0.12.2/30. R2 Gi0/1 10.0.23.1/30 faces R3 Gi0/0 10.0.23.2/30. R3 Gi0/1 192.168.30.1/24 faces SRV1 .10, gateway .1. R2 Gi0/1 intentionally has L3 MTU 1400. R1 has specific routes to the server LAN and R2–R3 transit; R2 has a prepared client-LAN route; R3 has a prepared R1–R2 transit route. Practice PC1 uses nonexistent gateway .254, R2 lacks its server-LAN route, R3 lacks its client-LAN return route, and TRACE-RETURN inbound on R2 Gi0/1 denies only Time Exceeded from R3 to PC1.
verificationNotes: Adds the second Network Assurance lab and updates the accessible two-lab badge. Existing IOS Debugging remains available. ENCOR has 24 labs; other section counts remain 3/6/9/4. Share links retain the current host, path and query.

Practice starts at 0 of 21. Six goals are live configuration/save checks and fifteen are earned packet/probe observations. The completed reference supplies six healthy outcomes with empty runtime and no pre-earned traffic or fault history. Every initial fault can be recreated from the completed reference and the same 21-task workflow completed.

Local PC1-to-R1 traffic can succeed despite the wrong default gateway. The gateway-fault observation requires actual ARP attempts for .254 and unresolved-neighbor remote packets. Correcting the gateway then reveals a real network-unreachable response from R2, rather than treating all unsuccessful pings as the same fault.

After R2's specific forward route is restored, requests reach SRV1 but replies stop at R3. R1's default egress-source ping from 10.0.12.1 can succeed via the prepared transit return route, while an explicit source of 192.168.10.1 fails. The task records both comparisons while the client-LAN return route is absent. R3's specific return route restores both host directions and the same explicit R1 source.

TRACE-RETURN sequence 10 filters returning R3 ICMP Time Exceeded only. Windows tracert can show a silent third hop and still reach SRV1 at hop 4, while end-to-end echo works. Repair removes only sequence 10, retaining sequence 20 permit ip any any and the original inbound binding; detaching the ACL cannot satisfy the intended policy.

Corrected IOS traceroute to send actual UDP datagrams rather than Echo requests. Default three-probe rows use TTL 1/2/3, a 40-byte IPv4 datagram, source ports in 32768–65535 and incrementing destination ports 33434–33442. Port, probe, TTL and source options affect actual datagrams. Returned ICMP Time Exceeded identifies intermediate hops; matched quoted UDP Port Unreachable completes the destination hop without a false !P error.

The UDP completion check correlates the quoted destination, protocol and port. It accepts a legitimate ICMP error sourced from the destination router's return interface when probing a loopback address. Active UDP listeners do not invent closed-port responses; suppressing destination ICMP unreachables causes timeout while Echo can still work.

Windows tracert remains ICMP-based, using actual TTL 1–4 Echo probes, returned ICMP Time Exceeded and a final Echo Reply. Bounded local probe-run metadata distinguishes completed tracert traffic from the explicit one-hop ping task; a trace's TTL-1 response alone cannot earn that ping outcome. These runtime records contain actual sent packet IDs and are discarded on export.

The intended path MTU remains 1400. A real 1500-byte DF probe elicits ICMP type 3/code 4 from R2 and IOS M; a 1400-byte DF probe receives a parent-linked Echo Reply. Non-DF or smaller ordinary pings do not substitute. Windows -l payload 1372 and IOS size 1400 both produce a 1400-byte IPv4 datagram. Existing ICMP error rate limiting can suppress individual probe responses.

Success observations correlate current FIB egress, every linked Ethernet hop and returned parent-linked replies. Error observations require actual received ICMP quoting real sent probes, the correct origin/drop event and the complete return path. Missing events, unrelated parents, default-route shortcuts, extra host routes, detached bindings, wrong addresses, outages and changed intended MTU are rejected.

All three router configurations must be saved in a healthy state. Portable exports retain fifteen earned observations, discard transient probe history, rebuild live routing and support fresh forwarding. Save drift and IOS reload are covered.

Scope is implemented IPv4 IOS/Windows ping and trace troubleshooting with static routing. There is no new claim of live CML capture, IPv6 lab coverage, reverse-path reconstruction from a forward trace, or hardware latency equivalence. CLI styling remains unchanged.

Fifteen browser scenarios passed with no page errors or external requests. Full21 workflows ran in light1440px and dark320px. Four other theme/viewport cases earned15 with the six initial fault observations still unearned. All six cases verified real YAML export/import into an empty offline browser profile, restored achievements, fresh forwarding, actual startup saves and unchanged golden CLI styling. Two arbitrary-origin share-link cases and seven existing catalog checks also passed.

references.title: Cisco: Understand the Extended Ping and Extended Traceroute Commands
references.relevance: Default egress-source versus explicit-source probes, bidirectional reachability, DF/datagram-size testing and UDP traceroute.

references.title: Cisco: Use the Traceroute Command on Operating Systems
references.relevance: IOS UDP ports and TTL progression versus Windows ICMP, destination Port Unreachable versus Echo Reply, and ICMP rate limiting.

references.title: RFC1812 §4.3.2.4: ICMP Message Source Address
references.relevance: A router-originated ICMP error may use its return interface address; loopback-target completion must correlate the quoted probe rather than requiring the ICMP source to equal the target.
